why: a release APK signed with the debug key installs and is not a release, and a line in a build log is not evidence of which key was used. This opens the file.

with_no_key.properties.what_that_means: Flutter's template signs a release with the shared debug key and says nothing. The build prints a block about it now, and this check reads the certificate out of the file rather than trusting the log.

without_--split-per-abi.what_that_means: 38.6 MB of engines and app images for phones the owner does not have. Every Android phone made this decade is arm64.

the_key_that_signs_these: a throwaway RSA key generated into /tmp for one build, thirty days' validity, a random password, deleted immediately afterwards along with the key.properties that pointed at it. It exists in this record only as the distinguished name below, which is how a reader can see that the signing config works and that it was not the shared debug key. No keystore, no password and no key.properties is in this repository or ever was; app/android/.gitignore covers all three.

signature.signed_by: CN=a throwaway key that proves the signing path, O=not for release, C=GB
signature.what_that_means: signed with a key that is not the shared debug one; keep the keystore, because only a build signed with it can update this one
